probe: When a deterministic effect resource can be deleted, what is the minimum durable identity-retention contract that still blocks an ambiguous-success retry from duplicating the effect? Compare immutable tombstone, generation/version namespace, and separate completion-token retention.
tested_scope: Documentation-level architectural falsification using only frozen CLEAN authority, own role-local LATEST state, and RFC 9110. No external effect, hosted compute, paid/trial API, protected authority, O/downstream/other-worker semantics, manual execution, scheduler mutation, or quota-bearing service was used.
observations: RFC 9110 If-None-Match:* prevents the method only while the origin server has a current representation for the target resource; when no current representation exists the condition is true.
RFC 9110 DELETE removes the association between the target resource and its current functionality, so deletion can make a previously occupied deterministic target absent again.
RFC 9110 method idempotence covers the intended effect requested by the client, not arbitrary implementation side effects; a server may still have non-idempotent side effects per request.
semantic_conclusion: MINIMUM_DURABLE_NONREUSE_IDENTITY_CONTRACT_ESTABLISHED: once the effect resource itself can disappear, deterministic URI plus PUT/If-None-Match:* is no longer sufficient across arbitrary replay. The minimum duplicate-safety contract is a durable non-reusable operation-identity marker that survives until the system can prove the operation can never be replayed again. If replay has no externally proven finite bound, the marker or an equivalent non-reuse reservation must persist indefinitely. A generation/version namespace alone is insufficient unless used generations remain durably reserved; otherwise deletion makes the same generation address creatable again, reducing the design back to tombstone/retention. A separate completion token is safety-equivalent to a tombstone when it is stable, non-reusable, authoritative, and atomically bound to the useful effect. Hidden/non-resource side effects remain unresolved unless the identity marker and those effects are transactionally coupled or independently idempotent.

immutable_tombstone_at_stable_operation_.success_probability: high under durable-retention and atomic-binding assumptions
immutable_tombstone_at_stable_operation_.duplicate_safety: high; survives deletion of the effect representation
immutable_tombstone_at_stable_operation_.integration_cost: low-to-medium; one minimal marker lookup/write path
immutable_tombstone_at_stable_operation_.quota_fragility: low in tested scope using existing lightweight repository transport only; no optional monthly/trial/paid quota consumed
immutable_tombstone_at_stable_operation_.hidden_side_effect_coverage: only when marker commit is atomically coupled to every non-idempotent useful side effect

generation_or_version_namespace_without_.duplicate_safety: fails after deletion because the same generation identity can become absent and creatable again

separate_completion_token_retention.duplicate_safety: high while token retention covers the complete replay horizon
separate_completion_token_retention.integration_cost: medium; separate token/effect binding and lookup
separate_completion_token_retention.quota_fragility: low in tested scope with lightweight transport only
separate_completion_token_retention.hidden_side_effect_coverage: requires atomic binding to all useful side effects

conflict_check: Exactly one bounded CLEAN Phase-1 child; own role-local state plus public RFC only; no other role/output/receipt, no scheduler mutation, no wait/poll/backoff/retry, and no optional second leaf.
frontier: r260 reduced full response replay to durable completion evidence plus authoritative read under atomic binding.
r261 showed deterministic resource identity can replace a separate idempotency registry while the exact effect resource persists.

r262 establishes that deletion breaks this equivalence: a durable non-reuse reservation/tombstone must outlive the replay horizon, and a namespace alone does not substitute for retained identity state.
Hidden or non-resource side effects still require atomic coupling or independent idempotence.
exact_continuation: Fresh-bootstrap current controls and reconstruct r262 from LATEST. Execute exactly one bounded CLEAN Phase-1 child: test whether any standards-level or protocol-level retry/redelivery bound can justify finite tombstone retention; compare finite-horizon retention plus safety margin against indefinite non-reuse when no such bound is proven, including clock-free criteria, duplicate safety, integration cost, zero-quota operation, and hidden-side-effect coverage. Use public specifications only if needed; preserve exact tested scope and do not start more than one leaf.
